decision.summary: Tom gave one month's notice by email on 10 Oct 2026. Under the Renters' Rights Act the notice is two months, so the earliest end date is 10 Dec 2026. I acknowledged the notice, asked the landlord about the earlier date, and started move-out against 10 Dec.

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? What is the earliest end date?
answers.answer: The notice is valid as written notice, but one month is too short. Tenants must give 2 months, so the earliest end date is 10 Dec 2026, counting from receipt on 10 Oct. 10 Nov is not valid unless the landlord agrees.

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: The landlord can agree to an earlier date in writing, for example 10 Nov. The tenant could also find a replacement tenant, but that still needs the landlord's agreement. I have asked the landlord; the tenant's rent runs until the agreed end date.

answers.question: What do you reply and what do you start?
answers.answer: I told Tom the valid date is 10 Dec and that we are asking the landlord about 10 Nov. I told him keys come back at checkout and that the deposit (£2,019, mydeposits) is returned after checkout once deductions are agreed or decided by the scheme, within 10 days of agreement. I told the landlord the steps started. I scheduled the landlord chase for 14 Oct and the checkout inspection and key return for 10 Dec.

actions_claimed.description: Acknowledged notice to tenant with valid end date, keys and deposit process
Asked landlord to accept or refuse earlier date and told him steps started
Follow-up 10 Dec for checkout inspection and key return

conflicts: Tenant says one month's notice, but the law requires two months.
assumptions: Email received 10 Oct counts as written notice served that day.
The tenancy is assured periodic, converted on 1 May 2026, per the CRM.

args.body:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for your email of 10 October. We've received your notice and are sorry to see you go, but congratulations on the new job.

Since May 2026 tenancies have no fixed end date, and the notice a tenant must give is two months in writing, not one. So the earliest end date is 10 December 2026, not 10 November. Your tenancy and rent continue until then. If the landlord agrees in writing to an earlier date we can shorten it. I'm asking him now and will tell you his answer; please don't plan on 10 November until we confirm it.

We're starting your move-out now against 10 December. We'll arrange a checkout inspection around that date and contact you with a time. Please hand back all keys to us at that inspection, or tell us if you'd prefer another way and we'll arrange it.

Your deposit (£2,019) is protected with mydeposits. After checkout, any deductions are agreed with you or decided by the scheme's free dispute service. Money is returned within 10 days of agreement.

You'll next hear from us once the landlord replies, and in any case by 14 October.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings

args.body:
Hi Ben,

Tom Achterberg at Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road gave written notice by email on 10 October, asking to leave on 10 November (new job in Manchester). Under the Renters' Rights Act the notice period is two months, so the earliest valid end date is 10 December 2026.

Decision for you: do you agree in writing to the earlier date of 10 November? Yes or no please, by 14 October. If we hear nothing, we'll keep 10 December.

Steps started: we've acknowledged the notice, told Tom the valid date, and are arranging the checkout inspection and key return against 10 December. The £2,019 deposit sits with mydeposits and is returned after checkout once deductions are agreed or decided by the scheme. Rent remains due until the tenancy ends.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings
